records.authority: Diggs et al. 1999, Flora of North Central Texas-Fab-Zygo.pdf

morphology.habit: Deciduous riparian tree to 30 m or more, broad open crown
morphology.leaves: Glabrous triangular (deltoid) to deltoid-ovate blades, serrate/crenate edge; petioles flattened 2.5–9 cm
morphology.fruits: Capsules 3–15 mm, opening to release cottony seeds
morphology.habitat: Streambanks, draws, ditches, newly bare moist substrate, reservoirs

records.diagnostic: Broad triangular toothed leaves on flattened petioles, riparian habit and cottony seeds
holds: Flora distinguishes subsp. deltoides (10–20 marginal teeth/side and glabrous bud scales) versus monilifera (5–10 and often hairy bud scales), with documented hybrid swarms
BONAP precise Hays zone not verified, though current local learner records may already address separately

records.flora_name: No species treatment in Diggs et al. 1999; often Populus trichocarpa Torr. & A.Gray ex Hook. in FNA and USFS
records.authority: Kew POWO 2026 taxonomy and USFS black cottonwood silvics
synonyms: Populus trichocarpa Torr. & A.Gray ex Hook.

morphology.habit: Large fast-growing deciduous black cottonwood, western North American native riparian tree
morphology.leaves: Broad pointed blades; typical black cottonwood has pale undersides, resinous buds and aromatic petioles; full verified quantitative treatment deferred
morphology.fruits: Poplar capsules releasing cotton-haired seeds; exact size pending FNA source review
morphology.habitat: Streams and moist bottomlands in Pacific Northwest/western mountain states

records.diagnostic: Black cottonwood of western North America; NOT a substitute for local eastern cottonwood P. deltoides
holds: Kew recognizes P. tristis and synonymizes P. trichocarpa, FNA and USDA frequently retain P. trichocarpa accepted; taxonomic-authority disagreement needs explicit source
Native range Western North America, no justified Hays target county pass
No 1999 regional original page or verified full numerical morphology

records.authority: Diggs et al. 1999, Flora of North Central Texas-Fab-Zygo.pdf

morphology.habit: Tree 20 m or more on wet stream banks
morphology.twigs: Reddish- to yellow-brown twigs, sharply pointed winter buds, overlapping bud scales
morphology.leaves: Narrow lanceolate blade 5–20 mm wide, green rather than markedly glaucous below; regularly fine teeth 0.3–2.1 mm apart at blade middle
morphology.petioles: 2–6 mm (up to 15 mm on new growth), usually bearing glands near blade
morphology.habitat: Streams, ditches, stock tanks, wet low areas

records.diagnostic: Pointed overlapping bud scales, fine regular teeth and green underside; differentiate rhizomatous S. exigua with wider teeth and rounded buds
holds: S. caroliniana hybridizes with S. nigra where adjacent; leaf underside and stamen counts important
BONAP county review independent of state range

records.authority: Diggs et al. 1999 + Kew POWO + H. Ballard species treatment

morphology.habit: Perennial with thick branching rootstock; clustered erect stems to 25(–35) cm in 1999 flora
morphology.leaves: Lower leaves opposite/whorled, upper alternate, narrow entire blades, specialized field study upper leaves to 41 × 2 mm
morphology.flowers: Axillary nodding on short pedicels, lower petal enlarged yellowish-green sometimes purple blotch, upper petals smaller purple/rose; no conventional violet spur
morphology.fruit: Modern study broad ovoid/globose capsule 4–6 mm, dark seeds around 2.5–3 mm
morphology.habitat: Prairie, rocky slopes and disturbed dry ground

records.diagnostic: Stemmed upright narrow leaves and tiny nodding mostly greenish two-sided flower unlike basal broad-leaved Viola
holds: Historical Hybanthus name and modern Pombalia explicitly reconciled
Precise 4–6 mm capsule from modern Ballard not printed 1999

records.flora_name: No confirmed original 1999 account; Gulf Coast reports often misidentified as V. missouriensis according to FNA
records.authority: Flora of North America, Viola affinis

morphology.habit: Acaulescent perennial violet with basal leaves and blue/violet spurred flowers
morphology.leaves: Leaf blade essentially hairless, except sometimes hairs on upper faces of basal lobes; broadly heart-shaped base, more regularly fine marginal teeth than V. missouriensis
morphology.flowers: Violet five-petaled spurred flowers, detailed internal beard characters need treatment check
morphology.fruit: Three-valved violet capsule, specific dimensions unverified
morphology.habitat: Usually moist sandy woods/alluvial forest in central-eastern USA

records.diagnostic: Deeply cordate regular-toothed leaf blades and specific hair placement vs more triangular scarcely toothed V. missouriensis
holds: FNA explicitly warns many Gulf Coastal records under V. affinis are actually V. missouriensis
Hays-area occurrence unverified; no BONAP approval or forced identification from flower color

records.authority: Diggs et al. 1999 and Flora of North America

morphology.leaves: Usually fully glabrous triangular blades at flowering, often longer than broad, tapering evenly to acuminate tip; truncate to slightly cordate base
morphology.flowers: Violet-blue to pale blue with white central patch and dark veins; beard hairs on lower lateral petals but not spurred petal
morphology.fruit: Yellow-green capsules speckled red-purple; brownish-orange to brown seeds
morphology.habitat: Moist settings, e and se TX into West Cross Timbers

records.diagnostic: Completely smooth, evenly tapering triangular blade with purple-spotted capsule vs broader hairier V. sororia and deeply heart-based V. affinis
holds: FNA maintains distinction but reports affinities and hybrids with other violets
Historical treatments disagree species vs variety of V. sororia

scope: Research-only: source-specific taxon, traits and holds; no photographs/species.json or site altered.
